transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I keep cutting people off and jumping into things before they’re finished talking or deciding, and it’s starting to mess up my job and my money. I really need to figure out why I can't seem to stop doing this before things get any worse.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'jumping into things' and if you've noticed any other impulsive behaviors, such as excessive spending or reckless driving?

By "jumping into things," I mean I constantly blurt out answers before people finish speaking and make snap decisions without hearing all the details first. I also struggle with impulsive spending on things like travel, vinyl records, and gear, which has really strained our family budget, though I don't have any issues with reckless driving.
Do you also find it difficult to focus on tasks, follow instructions, or make careless mistakes, in addition to your impulsive behaviors?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that, especially making careless mistakes at work like skipping a torque step or misreading decimals on a gauge even when I'm trying to be careful. I also have a really hard time following instructions because I'll drift off in my head while my wife or boss is talking, and then I have to ask them to repeat themselves.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, having trouble staying seated or engaging in quiet leisure activities, or do you feel more like your impulsivity is the main issue?

It is actually both, but they show up in different ways. I’m incredibly restless—I can't sit still for more than a few minutes without bouncing my leg, popping up during meetings, or feeling this crawling sensation inside like I'm constantly driven by a motor. But the impulsivity, like blurting things out and making snap financial decisions, is what is causing the most urgent trouble with my job and my marriage right now.
Did these symptoms of impulsivity, restlessness, and difficulty with focus and following instructions start when you were a child, or did they develop more recently in your life?

Honestly, these behaviors go all the way back to childhood—even in elementary school, I couldn't stay in my seat, constantly blurted out answers, and had report cards calling me "overactive" and "disruptive." However, it's only really started messing with my job and money over the last two years, ever since my company sped up the line and changed our bonus structure.

Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, consistently throughout your life, or have they waxed and waned over time?

I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I know I've always been hyperactive, but I haven't really thought about whether those specific focus and mistake issues have been constant or if they've come and gone over my life.

Can you think of any periods in your life, perhaps during high school, college, or earlier in your career, where you were able to focus and follow instructions without significant difficulty, or have you always struggled with these aspects to some degree?

I've definitely always struggled with these things to some degree, going all the way back to elementary school. I constantly got notes sent home for blurting out answers, talking over the teacher, and refusing to stay in my seat. My parents said my report cards always called me "overactive" and "disruptive," even though I was smart enough to do the schoolwork.
Can you describe how your hyperactivity and restlessness have impacted your daily life and relationships, particularly in terms of causing distress or impairment?

My constant fidgeting and jumping up during meetings makes people nervous at home and looks disrespectful to my bosses, which has led to write-ups and stalled my CNC certification. On top of that, not being able to sit still and constantly interrupting my wife during important budget talks has caused major arguments and severe stress over our bills.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you were able to sit through a long meeting or focus on a single task for an extended time without getting restless or making careless mistakes?

No, I've never really had a period in my life where I could sit still or focus without these issues. As far back as elementary school, I've always been overactive, unable to stay in my seat, and prone to rushing through things. While those traits have always been there, they only started causing severe, disruptive problems about two years ago when my job demands and financial pressures intensified.

Can you clarify if your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, have been consistently present since childhood, similar to your hyperactivity, or if they have become more pronounced or problematic over time?

While my high energy, inability to sit still, and tendency to blurt things out were highly visible in childhood, the careless mistakes and inattention have become much more problematic and noticeable over the last two years. This really escalated when my company increased the line speeds and introduced much stricter quality protocols, making those small details I used to blow past suddenly have major consequences.

Do you think your difficulties with following instructions and making careless mistakes are as troubling to you and impactful on your daily life as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity, or do you see one set of issues as more problematic than the other?

Both are incredibly destructive, but in different ways. The interrupting and jumping into things cause the most immediate tension and arguments with my wife, while the careless mistakes at work directly threaten my CNC certification and our income. They feel connected, though, because my mind is always racing ahead to the next thing.
Can you think of any situations or tasks where you're able to focus and avoid making careless mistakes, or are these difficulties present across all areas of your life?

These difficulties are present across almost all areas of my life, whether I'm on the line at work, sitting at the dinner table, or even stuck in traffic. I feel constantly restless and prone to making careless mistakes or jumping into things too quickly. Even when I'm working on projects I enjoy around the house, I find myself bouncing from one task to the next and I just can't relax.

Do you feel that your symptoms of inattention and impulsivity are equally severe and impactful on your daily life, or does one set of symptoms, such as hyperactivity or impulsivity, cause you more distress or impairment?

While both cause problems, the hyperactivity and impulsivity are definitely the most severe and cause the most damage to my marriage and job. My inability to stop myself from interrupting, making snap financial decisions, and needing to constantly move are my biggest hurdles. I do make attention errors, but that impulsive urge to act and speak before thinking is what really derails things.

Do you think your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, are as severe and impactful on your daily life as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity, which seem to be causing more immediate problems in your job and marriage?

They are actually just as severe, just in different ways. While the interrupting and jumping into things cause immediate arguments with my wife and friction with my bosses, the inattention—like skipping checklist steps and drifting off—directly leads to the quality errors and write-ups that are threatening my job and CNC certification.

Do you feel that your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity have been consistently present and problematic since childhood, or have they varied in severity over time, with some periods being more manageable than others?

They have definitely been around since childhood, with teachers always writing on my report cards that I was "overactive" and couldn't stay in my seat. However, their impact has varied over time—for years, my high energy was actually seen as an asset on the production floor. It is only over the last two years, since work rules got much stricter and financial pressures mounted, that they have become really unmanageable and problematic.

Looking back, do you feel that your difficulties with inattention, such as following instructions or making careless mistakes, have been as persistent and troublesome throughout your life as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity?

Looking back, the hyperactivity and impulsivity—like blurting things out and not being able to sit still—were definitely the most obvious and troublesome symptoms throughout my life, starting in childhood when everyone labeled me as 'overactive' and 'disruptive.' While I probably had some focus issues back then, the severe problems with making careless mistakes and drifting off have felt much more prominent and damaging in recent years, especially since the factory sped up the line and got stricter.

Do you think the severity of your inattention symptoms, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, is comparable to the severity of your hyperactivity and impulsivity symptoms, or does one set of symptoms clearly cause more problems in your daily life?

They are definitely comparable in damage, though they show up in different ways. The impulsivity and interrupting are what pushed me to get help because they are ruining my marriage and budget, but the inattention is just as dangerous because careless mistakes on the line directly threaten my job security. They both cause severe problems, even if the impulsiveness feels more disruptive day-to-day.

Do you feel that your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, have become more prominent or equally problematic compared to your hyperactivity and impulsivity symptoms over the last two years, considering the changes in your job demands and financial pressures?

Yes, they have absolutely become equally problematic over the last two years. While my hyperactivity and interrupting have always been a constant struggle, the faster line speeds and strict quality protocols at work have really exposed my inattention, leading to costly careless mistakes and skipped checklist steps. Now, missing those details is just as damaging to my job and wallet as my impulsivity.

Do you think the impact of your inattention symptoms on your daily life and relationships is now as significant as the impact of your hyperactivity and impulsivity symptoms, given the recent changes in your work environment and financial situation?

Yes, they’ve become a double whammy causing equal damage now. While my impulsivity and snap spending cause immediate fights with my wife and bosses, the inattention—like skipping torque steps and zoning out during budget talks—directly costs me bonuses and stalls my CNC certification. One gets me into trouble, and the other keeps me from fixing my mistakes at work.

Do you believe that if you could better manage your impulsivity, your inattention symptoms, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, would also improve, or do you think they are largely independent of each other?

I definitely think they are connected, because my tendency to rush ahead is exactly why I make careless mistakes and miss instructions. For instance, I skip steps on the line because my mind is already racing to the next part, or I'll cut people off and then realize I missed half of what they actually said. If I could manage that impulse to jump ahead, I think I'd finally be able to slow down and pay better attention.

Do you feel that your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, have been consistently problematic throughout your life, similar to your hyperactivity and impulsivity, or have they become more prominent and problematic over time, especially with the recent changes in your job and financial situation?

The hyperactivity and impulsivity have definitely been there since childhood, as my school reports always labeled me "overactive" and "disruptive" even though I was smart enough to get by. However, the inattention symptoms—like missing checklist details and drifting off during important conversations—have become much more prominent and problematic over the last two years. The faster line speeds, stricter work protocols, and financial stress at home have really exposed those focus issues and made them much more damaging.
Do you think your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are equally severe and impactful on your daily life, or does one set of symptoms clearly cause more distress or impairment?

While both are definitely problematic, the hyperactivity and impulsivity are what cause the most immediate distress and conflict in my life. I do have inattentive moments like drifting off or missing small details on the line, but the "driven by a motor" feeling and my inability to stop myself from jumping into things and interrupting are what really derail my conversations, harm my marriage, and get me into trouble.

Can you describe any situations or tasks where you feel your inattention symptoms, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, are less severe or more manageable compared to your hyperactivity and impulsivity symptoms?

I'm not really sure, to be honest, as I haven't noticed any situations where the inattention is easier to manage. Both the constant urge to move or interrupt and the careless mistakes feel pretty overwhelming right now, and they both seem to cause me constant trouble no matter what I'm doing.

Do you feel that your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are equally responsive to situational factors, such as stress or environment, or does one set of symptoms seem more sensitive to changes in your surroundings?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't ever thought about comparing them that way. All I know is that both of them seem to flare up and get a lot worse when I'm under pressure at work or stressed about our money situation.

Do you think your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, have been consistently as severe as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity throughout your life, or have they varied in severity over time?

I'm not entirely sure how they compare over my whole life. As a kid, the hyperactivity and impulsivity, like not staying in my seat and blurting things out, were what everyone noticed and got me in trouble, whereas the careless mistakes and trouble listening have felt much more prominent and problematic recently since my job became more demanding. I guess I haven't really thought about which one has been consistently worse over time.

Do you feel that your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, are now as severe and impactful as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity, considering how they both affect your daily life and relationships?

Yes, they are absolutely equally severe now, but they hurt me in different ways. The inattention, like skipping checklist steps on the line and zoning out when my wife is talking, directly costs us money, risks my bonuses, and stalls my CNC certification. Meanwhile, my hyperactivity and impulsivity, like interrupting people, snap spending, and not being able to sit still, drive the constant fights at home and get me written up, teaming up to ruin my marriage and financial stability.

Do you feel that your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, have been consistently as severe as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity throughout your entire life, or have they become more comparable in severity only recently?

Growing up, the hyperactivity and impulsivity were definitely the main issues; I was always the "overactive" and "disruptive" kid who couldn't sit still or stop blurting things out, even though I was smart enough to get through the schoolwork. The inattention and careless mistakes have only become a comparable, major problem over the last two years. That's when the increased line speeds, strict safety checklists, and financial pressures at work and home really started exposing those focus issues.

Do you think your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty following instructions or making careless mistakes, have become as severe as your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity over the last two years, considering how they both impact your job and marriage?

Yes, they have absolutely become equally severe and destructive over the last two years. My inattention—like making careless decimal errors on the line and zoning out when my wife or boss talks—is just as damaging to my job and marriage as my impulsive cutting people off and rash spending. It is incredibly frustrating that both sides of this problem are hitting my wallet and my relationship at the exact same time.

Do you think your symptoms of hyperactivity, such as restlessness and fidgeting, are more prominent and troublesome than your impulsive behaviors, such as interrupting others and making snap decisions?

While the constant physical restlessness and fidgeting are annoying, the impulsive behaviors like interrupting and making snap decisions are definitely much more troublesome. The physical stuff mostly just makes other people nervous, but my impulsivity is what is actually threatening my job, hurting our finances, and causing major fights with my wife.
Do you think your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are equally responsive to treatment, or do you think one set of symptoms might be more challenging to manage than the other?

I'm really not sure how they would respond to treatment, since I haven't actually started any yet. I haven't really thought about which one might be harder to manage, I'm just hoping to find some way to get both of them under control.
